tara: heads-up — saw a flurry of onboarding tickets where the types in our JS SDK look fine in VSCode but collapse to `any` after people bundle for edge. putting notes here so we don't ship more confusing samples.
aldo: ugh. any repro or common tsconfig folks are using?
tara: yes, small repro in a customer sample:
```ts
// samples/edge-quick/src/handler.ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
export default async function handler(req: Request) {
  const out = await client.generate<{ text: string }>({ prompt: 'ping' });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(out));
}
```
common tsconfig from the report:
```json
{ "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2020", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "isolatedModules": true, "declaration": true, "esModuleInterop": false } }
```
wei: that matches the pattern we've seen. twofold failure: (1) type surfaces using many overloads + conditional types cause `declaration` artifacts that esbuild can't parse -> it falls back to any; (2) consumers without `esModuleInterop` hit default/named import mismatch at runtime.
jules: quick idea — publish a compatibility dts that exposes a single canonical exported signature for the most-used methods (generate/embed) and keep the overloads only in internal paths so bundlers get a stable entrypoint.
aldo: i like that. also add a sample tsconfig snippet in the README to reduce first-run pain: recommend `esModuleInterop: true` and `module: 'NodeNext'` for modern edge runtimes.
tara: another nuance: overload order affects inference. some customers relied on the old overload order to get a narrow inferred type. if we change shape, we should document the migration.
wei: long-term fix: change outward-facing API to single generic signatures so `isolatedModules`/esbuild never have to resolve multiple overloads. example sketch: `generate<T = string | Record<string, unknown>>(opts: GenerateOptions): Promise<T>` and `embed<T = unknown>(opts: { input: string | string[] } & EmbedOptions): Promise<T[]>`. keeps inference and avoids overload ordering surprises.
jules: CI add: run `tsc --noEmit` with `isolatedModules: true` and run an esbuild bundle step in the matrix (edge target). block if declaration parsing or bundle fails.
docs-bot: note added to samples/edge-quick/README.md with recommended tsconfig and quick esbuild command: `esbuild src/handler.ts --bundle --platform=browser --format=esm`.
ci-bot: current branch edge-typing-fix shows failing typecheck for the sample: https://ci.internal/redsdk/5542 (types + bundle). @jules assigned.
jules: opening PR #3191 with: - canonical exported generics for public API - `types/compat.d.ts` for legacy overloads - package.json `types` set to `dist/index.d.ts` - sample README + tsconfig recommendations - CI matrix job for tsc+esbuild smoke.
tara: please also add a short BREAKING.md entry noting customers that relied on overload-order inference may see different inferred types and how to pin the old behavior.
aldo: small test we should run after merge: smoke import test for CJS and ESM (Node + bun?), with a tiny sample that imports both `require('@redwood/inference')` and `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` to ensure interop.
wei: +1. i'll script a quick internal smoke-run against two prod routes that use deep generic shapes (routing + typed prompts) once PR merges.
jules: PR opened #3191 and added the runnable minimal repro under `samples/edge-quick` for external contributors to validate locally. tagging @tara @aldo for review.
tara: perfect. thanks everyone — this should cut down onboarding tickets and rescue a lot of confusing error reports. :thumbsup:
